name: CONAGHAN, Patrick (Pat) John

headline.note: The official chronology identifies public NSW Police service from 1990 to 2001 and private legal practice from 2001 to 2019, but only at year precision and without substantive full-time evidence. Council office, campaigning, study and federal elected office are excluded. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official occupation extract records NSW Police constable service from 1990 to 1993. Current first-party and Nationals biographies corroborate police service. Exact appointment dates, hours, leave and study overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is clear, but year-only boundaries and unproven substantive full-time status do not support an exact headline duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract records Crime Squad detective service from 1993 to 1997; secondary biographical material corroborates transfer from Kempsey to Sydney and detective work. Exact dates, unit, hours, leave and study overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is clear, but no exact substantive full-time interval is established.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract records NSW Police prosecutor service from 1997 to 2001, corroborated by current and secondary biographies. Exact appointment and cessation dates, hours, leave and transition to private practice are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is clear, but year-only boundaries and unproven substantive full-time status do not support an exact headline duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary biographical material identifies an LLB from the University of New England. Enrolment and completion dates, load and overlap with police service are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract records solicitor work from 2001 to 2019. Secondary material says Conaghan established his own criminal-defence practice, and a public professional-profile result names Conaghan Lawyers. ABN Lookup records the Australian private company as active from 6 July 2001. The corporate registration date does not prove Conaghan's exact work start; exact cessation, hours, ownership period, leave and campaign overlap remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private control and self-employment are supported, but year-only work boundaries and unproven substantive full-time status prevent an exact headline duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary material citing North Sydney Council records the council term from 27 March 2004 to 13 September 2008. Remuneration, hours and overlap with legal practice are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected local-government office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Contemporaneous regional reporting records Nationals preselection on 3 November 2018; the frozen roster records House service from 18 May 2019. Pay, hours, legal-practice leave and exact active campaign period are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party and campaign activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster establishes House service from 18 May 2019, corroborated by current first-party and Nationals biographies. Parliamentary roles are nested within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: The frozen official extract supplies a continuous year-level occupation sequence from 1990 to parliamentary entry but not exact transitions or working hours.
The private company's registration date corroborates legal-entity existence and control, not the exact first day of Conaghan's work.
Police ranks and professional titles are not treated as proof of substantive full-time status.
Council service overlapped private legal practice and is excluded rather than double-counted.
open_questions: What were the exact NSW Police appointment, transfer, promotion and cessation dates, hours and leave?
What were the UNE law-study dates, load and overlap with police service?
Did Conaghan work for another legal employer before or alongside Conaghan Lawyers, and what were the exact practice dates, ownership, hours and leave?
What were the council remuneration and hours and the legal-practice overlap?
What were the campaign's paid status, hours and exact leave/cessation arrangements with the law practice?
